items.title: Date and time parity: sign of clock differences, natural display, IANA/city zones, relative dates, workdays, timecode
items.body:
Part of #227.

## Evidence

| Expression | Source | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `5pm - 7pm` | Soulver | 2 hours | **-2 hours** |
| `3am - 4pm` | Soulver | 13 hours | **-13 hours** |
| `days between 3 March and 30 May` | Soulver | 88 days | **-88 days** |
| `January 10 - February 5` | Soulver | 3 weeks 5 days | -26 days |
| `10 June + 3 weeks` | Soulver | 1 July | 2026-07-01 |
| `Feb 28 + 1 month` | Soulver | 28 March | 2026-03-28 |
| `2am PST to GMT` | Soulver | 10:00 am | 10:00:00 GMT |
| `00:12:05 − 00:04:09` | Soulver | 00:07:56 | 7 minutes, 56 seconds |
| `30 fps × 3 minutes` | Soulver | 5,400 frames | **90 FPS** |
| `yesterday - 8 weeks 3 days`, `Yesterday + 1 week` | Soulver | | `Unexpected identifier: yesterday` |
| `time in Paris`, `time in Tokyo`, `5pm ldn in sf` | Soulver/Raycast | | `Could not parse 'time'` |
| `monday in 3 weeks`, `next friday`, `workdays until 25 December` | Raycast/Soulver | | unsupported (`workdays` 2 rows) |
| `Invalid datetime format` | | | 24 rows |

The sign difference is the one that matters: Soulver, Numi and Raycast report the absolute span for "between"/"from-to" style phrases while keeping the sign for explicit subtraction of later from earlier dates; this project negates both.

## Acceptance criteria

- `between`, `from … to …`, `until`, and `a - b` with clock times follow the competitor convention documented in the Soulver dates page; a `--iso` flag or result metadata keeps the machine-readable form.
- Date results display in the input style (`1 July`, `12 February 2020`) with ISO available in the result object.
- IANA zones and city names (`Europe/London`, `Paris`, `Tokyo`, `ldn`, `sf`) via `chrono-tz` 0.10.4 plus a city table; `time in <city>`.
- Relative dates with a caller-supplied reference instant: `yesterday`, `tomorrow`, `next monday`, `monday in 3 weeks`, `3 weeks ago`, `in 2 months`; `workdays`/`weekdays` arithmetic with a configurable weekend.
- Lap times `00:12:05`, timecode `01:00:00:00 @ 25 fps`, `fps × duration = frames`.

## Solution options

1. Extend `src/grammar/datetime_grammar.rs` with a relative-date layer and display mode; add `chrono-tz` behind a feature flag to limit WASM size. Recommended.
2. `rust_dateparser` / `dateparser` crates. Reference only (see issue-220 audit): they do not preserve the AST.

## Blockers

- Blocked by: #229.

items.title: Fix #247, #254, #258: native JS engine at parity, Rust generated from JS, JS-first CI
items.body:
## Summary

As #260 asks, this one PR covers #247, #254 and #258.

Fixes #260
Fixes #247
Fixes #254
Fixes #258

### #247 and #258
The case studies are in `docs/case-studies/issue-247` and `docs/case-studies/issue-258`, with fixes and regression tests.

### #254: JavaScript first, Rust gated
- **R1: native JS engine.** `js/` (`link-calculator`) is a dependency-free, module-by-module port of the Rust engine.
  - It includes exact ports of the `rust_decimal`, `num-rational`, libm 0.2.16 and `chrono` subsets.
  - `npm run parity` matches the Rust goldens on **all 2474** cases of `parity/corpus.json`.
  - Parity runs on Node 20, Node 24 and Bun in the JS stage, and again in the Rust stage's test job; `tests/parity_goldens.rs` checks the Rust side.
  - `web/` now runs on `link-calculator/wasm` (the same API as `src/wasm.rs`) instead of the wasm-pack build.
- **R2: Rust generated from JS.**
  - `js/scripts/translate-rust.mjs` translates `js/src` with link-foundation/meta-language, at the commit pinned in a ledger, into `js/rust-generated/`.
  - 629 items translate. Each of the 1512 carried items is listed in `js/translation-allowlist.lino` with its upstream blocker.
  - `--verify` runs in `npm test`. The JS-stage job **JS to Rust Translation** retranslates and diffs (`--check`).
  - The generated Rust is not compiled yet, so the hand-written crate is still what ships.
- **R3: JS stage first.**
  - `release.yml` holds only JavaScript, Python and shell jobs, including **Web Build**, which runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, the build and the Playwright e2e suite.
  - `rust-stage` calls `rust.yml` only after every JS job passed.
  - `scripts/check-javascript-first.mjs` enforces this, and `.github/main-ruleset.json` makes both stages required checks. An admin has to apply the ruleset with `gh api -X POST repos/link-assistant/calculator/rulesets --input .github/main-ruleset.json`; until then the check fails on `main` with that instruction.
- **R4: cancellation.** Every JS job uses `cancel-in-progress: true`. The Rust stage queues per branch and never cancels. `scripts/ci-runs-per-pr.mjs` measures runs per PR.
- **R5: bounded builds.** Added `.cargo/config.toml`, `scripts/bounded-cargo.mjs` (job count, memory and disk caps) and the `setup-rust` action with a per-job exact cache.
- **R6: push discipline.** Added `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` and `scripts/ci-push-gate.mjs`.
- **R7: template checks.** Added the links, security and workflows (actionlint and zizmor) workflows, Dependabot with a cooldown, `rust-toolchain.toml` and SHA-pinned actions.
- **Versioning.** `scripts/sync-js-version.mjs` keeps `js/` at Cargo.toml's version; the release scripts run it and Script Checks verifies it.

The details are in `docs/case-studies/issue-254/README.md`.

### Upstream and follow-ups
- Filed rust-lang/compiler-builtins#1353: the generic `fma` loses its sticky bit, which affects `f64::mul_add` on wasm32.
- meta-language: carried items reference the existing issues #204–#213 and #223. Ten more reports (A–J) are drafted in `experiments/issue-254/meta-language/README.md` §5.2 and are not filed yet; they are marked `drafted:X` in the allowlist.
- Out of scope, found while porting: `Rational::from_f64` panics for magnitudes beyond `i128` (for example `1e39`). This needs a follow-up issue.

### How to verify
```sh
cd js && npm ci && npm test && npm run parity && npm run smoke
node scripts/translate-rust.mjs --verify
cd ../web && npm ci && npm test && npm run build && npx playwright test
node scripts/check-javascript-first.mjs && node --test scripts/*.test.mjs
```


### CodeQL
This PR introduced four alerts, and all four are fixed:
- **Cache poisoning:** meta-language is now fetched at the validated pinned commit in a shell step.
- **ReDoS (2 alerts):** the float regex in `num.js` is now unambiguous, and `delta.js` trims trailing zeros without a regex.
- **Dynamic dispatch:** the web worker now picks rate fetchers from a fixed list of sources.

Alerts #1–#4 were already open on `main` and are unchanged. The warning about the missing `security.yml:codeql/language:rust` configuration is expected, because CodeQL for Rust moved into `rust.yml`.

items.title: Fix #222, #223, #224: exact arithmetic and number words, latest dependencies with CI freshness check, bundled currency rates
items.body:
## Summary

This one PR resolves every open issue (#222, #223, #224), as #225 requires.

Fixes #222
Fixes #223
Fixes #224
Fixes #225

---

## #224: `35usd- 200cny- 1hkd` → "Cannot convert HKD to USD: No exchange rate available"

**Reproduce (on `main`):** `cargo run -- "35usd- 200cny- 1hkd"`. The same thing happens in the web app until the live ECB fetch succeeds.

**Root cause:** a fresh `Calculator` only knew 11 hardcoded fallback rates (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CNY, RUB, INR, CLF, VND, KZT). HKD, AUD, CAD, SEK and the other ECB currencies needed the live fetch, even though the repository already ships daily central-bank rates in `data/currency/*.lino`.

**Fix:**
- `build.rs` embeds the latest row of every `data/currency/*.lino` file. `CurrencyDatabase::new()` uses it only for currencies that have no fallback rate. The source and date shown in the steps are real (e.g. `frankfurter.dev (ECB)`), and live API rates still override them.
- Applied everywhere it was relevant:
  - Every bundled ECB currency converts, including non-USD cross pairs.
  - The **SEK** (Swedish krona) vs German `sek` (seconds) collision is resolved: uppercase ISO codes are currencies, and lowercase `sek` stays a duration unless the conversion target is a currency.
- The CLI gained a one-shot mode (`link-calculator "<expr>"`). It also no longer spins forever when stdin hits EOF.

**Tests:** `tests/issue_224_bundled_fallback_rates_tests.rs` covers:
- the exact input;
- the spaced input;
- all 16 ECB currencies → USD and EUR;
- the rate source and date in the steps;
- existing defaults unchanged;
- the API override;
- the SEK/sek cases.

---

## #223: dependencies at latest releases, publish 0.21.0, freshness in CI

| Req | Status |
|---|---|
| **R1** update `num-bigint` 0.4 → 0.5, `thiserror` 1 → 2 | Done |
| **R2** `cargo update` | Done; `cargo update --dry-run` reports nothing pending |
| **R3** CI fails on outdated direct dependencies | Done (Rust **and** JavaScript) |
| **R4** publish 0.21.0 | The pipeline is fixed; it publishes when this PR is merged (see below) |

**Breaking changes handled (R1):**
- `num-bigint` 0.5: the removed and changed APIs are the `rand` integration and some deprecated items. This crate uses neither, so no source changes were needed.
- `num-rational` 0.4 (the latest release) enables a `num-bigint` feature that pins **num-bigint 0.4**. That feature is now disabled (`default-features = false, features = ["std"]`). `Ratio<T>` is generic, so `Ratio<BigInt>` works unchanged with num-bigint 0.5 and there is only one copy of num-bigint.
- `thiserror` 2: this crate's derives are unaffected by the 2.0 changes (raw-identifier formatting, and the `std` requirement now behind a default feature). No code changes were needed.
- Verified the issue's own test: a fresh crate depending on this branch plus `num-bigint = "0.5"` and `thiserror = "2"` prints *nothing* for `cargo tree -d -e normal` (no duplicates at all). The probe manifest is in `experiments/consumer-probe-Cargo.toml`.

**Why 0.21.0 was never published (R4), root cause:**
1. A stray `wasm-pack-*.tar.gz` and an extracted wasm-pack binary (~10 MB) were committed to the repository root and packaged into the `.crate`, so crates.io rejected the upload (`413 Payload Too Large`).
2. `scripts/publish-crate.mjs` didn't check `cargo publish`'s exit code, so the workflow reported success anyway.

Fixed by:
- removing the files and downloading wasm-pack outside the checkout;
- adding an explicit `include` list to `Cargo.toml` (the `.crate` is now ~650 KB);
- making the publish script fail on errors.

`main` is at 0.21.0 and this PR adds `changelog.d` fragments (`bump: minor`), so the release workflow publishes the next version on merge. I have no crates.io credentials, so publishing has to happen through that workflow.

**R3: new `dependency-freshness` CI job** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`), driven by `scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs`:
- Rust:
  - `cargo outdated --root-deps-only --format json` checks the direct dependencies.
  - `cargo update --dry-run` must report no pending lockfile updates.
- JavaScript: `npm outdated --json` in `web/`.
- A dependency that can't be updated yet is allowed only when its blocker is documented with a GitHub issue URL:
  - in `Cargo.toml`, as a comment on the dependency line or on the comment line directly above it;
  - in `package.json`, which has no comments, in a `dependencyBlockers` map.
- The build job also fails if the packaged `.crate` reaches the 10 MiB crates.io limit, so the 413 can't come back.
- Unit tests: `scripts/check-dependency-freshness.test.mjs`.

**JavaScript dependencies (web/):** every package in `web/` is now at its latest release, so `npm outdated` exits 0. Major versions: React 19, Vite 8, Vitest 5, TypeScript 7, jsdom 30, jest-dom 7, i18next 26, react-i18next 17, KaTeX 0.19, links-notation 0.22, lino-objects-codec 0.8, @vitejs/plugin-react 6 and browser-commander 0.21.

Breaking changes handled:
- **TypeScript 7** removed `baseUrl` (TS5102). Dropped it; `paths` is already relative.
- **jest-dom 7** no longer adds its matchers to Vitest's types. The test setup now imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`.
- **Vite 8** denies `../../../data/examples.lino?raw` (outside `web/`). Added `server.fs.allow` for the repository root in both Vite configs, and replaced `__dirname` with `import.meta.dirname`.
- `vite-plugin-top-level-await` was removed because the `esnext` target supports top-level await natively. It was also the source of both `npm audit` warnings, and audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities. `@types/katex` was removed because KaTeX 0.19 ships its own types.
- **browser-commander 0.21** launches the system Chrome by default. The screenshot script now passes `launch: 'engine'`, the Playwright-managed launcher the library's docs give for CI/headless use.
- React 19, i18next 26, react-i18next 17, KaTeX 0.19, links-notation 0.22 and lino-objects-codec 0.8 needed no source changes.
- **Node 24 in CI:** Vitest 5, jsdom 30, jest-dom 7, lino-objects-codec 0.8 and browser-commander 0.21 need Node ≥ 22, so every workflow now uses Node 24 (LTS), and `web/package.json` declares `engines.node >= 22.12`.

Results on Node 24:
- `tsc --noEmit` passes; `npm test` passes 229/229; `npm run build` passes.
- Playwright e2e: the same 6 tests (theme toggle, URL history, textarea auto-resize) fail with the *old* dependencies too, so the upgrade doesn't cause them. Two currency tests are flaky because they depend on the network.
- Known limit: `npm run lint` was already broken on `main`. ESLint was never installed and CI doesn't run it. typescript-eslint can't support TypeScript 7 until 7.1 ([typescript-eslint#12518](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/12518)), so adding ESLint is left out of this PR.

**CI on `main` was also broken by Rust 1.99** (stable since 2026-09-28): its new `clippy::assert_is_empty` lint failed the Lint job. Fixed in all 10 places in `src/` and `tests/`; checked with clippy 1.98 and 1.99.

---

## #222: general expression evaluation without a consumer-side fallback

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Exact arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic | Done. `123123980921093128 * 2348023048230429324` and `10^100` are exact. Fixed `30!` returning `0` (factorial is now `BigInt`). Results outside the Decimal range raise an overflow error instead of a silent `0`. Exact values below 1e-28 now show in scientific notation (`10^-40` → `1e-40`, previously `0`) |
| Linear equations in one unknown | Already supported (`2x + 3 = 11` → `x = 4`); covered by conformance tests |
| Spelled numbers and operator words **as data** | Done: `data/words/arithmetic-words.lino` (see below) |
| `no_std` + `alloc` | **Not implemented**; evidence and plan below. The underlying goal (the evaluator running in WASM workers) is already met |
| Step trace | Already present in `CalculationResult.steps`; covered by tests |

Precedence fix found by the conformance suite: `-2^2` returned `4`. Unary minus now binds looser than `^`, so `-2^2 = -4`, `-2² = -4` and `2 * -3^2 = -18`. Unicode comparison signs `≠ ≤ ≥` were added next to `!= <= >=`.

**Number and operator words as a data table:**
- `data/words/arithmetic-words.lino` uses Links Notation, one link per word: `(number en 20 'twenty')`, `(scale ru 1000 'тысяч')`, `(operator zh + '加上')`.
- It covers English, Russian, Spanish, Hindi and Chinese: number words, scale words (hundred/thousand/million/billion, тысяча, mil, हज़ार, 万, …) and operator phrases (`multiplied by`, `to the power of`, `разделить на`, `dividido entre`, `गुणा`, `除以`, …).
- `src/grammar/arithmetic_words.rs` loads the table once (`include_str!` + `OnceLock`) and validates it. Malformed links and conflicting meanings are rejected by tests.
- The hardcoded English operator keywords in the lexer and the special `by` handling in the parser are replaced by the table. Adding a language now means editing data, not code.
- Composition is exact:
  - `twenty three` = 23 and `two thousand five hundred` = 2500;
  - `one billion^4` stays exact;
  - `двадцать три` = 23 and `二十三` = 23;
  - unspaced Chinese works: `一百除以四` = 25.
- Ambiguous cases keep their existing meaning:
  - `mod(17, 5)` and `17 mod 5`;
  - `10 per 4`;
  - `1 USD в RUB`;
  - French `once` (ounce);
  - CJK units such as `千克`;
  - month names such as `十二月`;
  - uppercase currency codes such as `ONE`, `DOS` and `MIL`.

**`no_std`: why it is not in this PR:**
- The dependencies are not the obstacle: `regex`, `num-bigint` 0.5, `num-rational`, `rust_decimal` and `thiserror` 2 all support `no_std` + `alloc`.
- The blockers are in the crate itself (~17k lines):
  - `f64` transcendental functions (sin, ln, exp, …) need `libm` without `std`;
  - about 20 uses of `std::collections::HashMap` (they would move to `hashbrown`);
  - `chrono`'s clock (`now`) for date and time expressions;
  - the `wasm-bindgen`/`web-sys` currency and crypto fetch layers.
- Reaching it means a `std` default feature that gates those parts. That is a crate-wide refactor touching most modules, and too large to do safely next to the fixes above.
- The motivating goal already works today:
  - `cargo build --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release` succeeds;
  - CI builds the wasm package with wasm-pack;
  - `web/src/worker.ts` runs the evaluator inside a **Web Worker**.
- Plan for the follow-up: a `std` default feature, `hashbrown`, `libm`, `core::fmt`/`alloc` imports, and the datetime clock and network APIs behind `std`.

**Tests:**
- `tests/issue_222_exact_arithmetic_tests.rs`: big integers, powers, precedence, factorial, overflow errors, the formal-ai fallback expressions, linear equations and the step trace.
- `tests/issue_222_number_words_tests.rs`: formal-ai's number-word expressions in en/ru/hi/zh/es, compound numbers, preserved meanings, `≠ ≤ ≥` and tiny exact values.
- Unit tests in `src/grammar/arithmetic_words.rs`.

**Libraries considered:**
- `num-bigint`/`num-rational`: already used, now exact everywhere.
- `rust_decimal`: its 28-digit limit is why tiny values now use rationals for display.
- `meval`/`evalexpr`/`fasteval`: limited to f64 (and i64), so not exact; rejected.
- Spelled-number crates such as `text2num`: they cover parsing only and fewer languages, and are code-driven. The issue explicitly asked for data tables.

---

## How to verify locally

```bash
cargo fmt --check
RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
cargo test
node --test scripts/*.test.mjs
node scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs   # needs cargo-outdated
cargo run -- "35usd- 200cny- 1hkd"
cargo run -- "two thousand five hundred plus twenty three"
cargo run -- "123123980921093128 * 2348023048230429324"
```

items.title: fix: calendar month arithmetic and full duration unit names
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #128.

Two bugs in `(17 февраля 2027) - 6 месяцев`:

- **Wrong day**: result was `2026-08-21`, should be `2026-08-17`
- **Abbreviations**: steps/lino showed `6 mo` instead of `6 months`

## Root Causes

### Bug 1 — Seconds-based month arithmetic

`src/types/unit.rs` `DurationUnit::to_secs` converted months/years to a fixed number of seconds:

```rust
// Before
Self::Months => value * 2_592_000.0,  // 30 days (wrong)
Self::Years  => value * 31_536_000.0, // 365 days (wrong)
```

`2027-02-17 - 180 days = 2026-08-21` ≠ `2026-08-17` (correct calendar result).

### Bug 2 — Abbreviation display

`DurationUnit::Display` showed `"mo"`, `"y"`, `"h"`, etc.

## Fixes

### Fix 1 — Calendar arithmetic via `chrono::Months`

Added `DateTime::add_calendar_months(i32)` in `src/types/datetime.rs`:

```rust
pub fn add_calendar_months(&self, months: i32) -> Self {
    let naive = self.inner.naive_utc();
    let new_naive = if months >= 0 {
        naive.checked_add_months(Months::new(months as u32)).unwrap_or(naive)
    } else {
        naive.checked_sub_months(Months::new((-months) as u32)).unwrap_or(naive)
    };
    // ...
}
```

Added `add_calendar_months_or_duration` helper in `src/types/value.rs` that dispatches on `Months`/`Years` (calendar) vs all other units (seconds). All four `DateTime ± duration-unit` match arms in `add_at_date` / `subtract_at_date` now use it.

Month-end clamping is handled by chrono (e.g. `31 Jan + 1 month → 28 Feb`).

### Fix 2 — Full English word display

Updated `DurationUnit::Display` to return full words (`months`, `years`, `days`, …).

## Tests

8 new tests in `tests/issue_128_calendar_month_arithmetic_tests.rs`:

| Test | What it checks |
|------|----------------|
| `test_issue_128_exact_day_preserved_russian` | `17 февраля 2027 - 6 месяцев = 2026-08-17` |
| `test_issue_128_exact_day_preserved_english` | `17 February 2027 - 6 months = 2026-08-17` |
| `test_issue_128_exact_day_preserved_add_months` | `17 August 2026 + 6 months = 2027-02-17` |
| `test_issue_128_month_end_clamping` | `31 January 2027 + 1 month = 2027-02-28` |
| `test_issue_128_year_arithmetic_preserves_day` | `17 февраля 2024 + 1 год = 2025-02-17` |
| `test_issue_128_subtract_year_preserves_day` | `15 марта 2025 - 2 года = 2023-03-15` |
| `test_issue_128_steps_show_full_word_months` | Steps contain `"6 months"` not `"6 mo"` |
| `test_issue_128_russian_steps_show_full_word_months` | Russian input → full English word in steps |

All 752 existing + 8 new tests pass (`cargo test`: 0 failures).

## Case Study

Deep root-cause analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-128/README.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-128/README.md)

---

items.title: feat: Implement Link Calculator with Rust WASM + React frontend
items.body:
## Summary

Implements the Link Calculator application as specified in issue #1. This PR provides:

- **Rust WebAssembly core** with grammar-based expression parsing
- **React frontend** with Web Worker for async calculations
- **GitHub Pages deployment** via GitHub Actions

## Screenshots

### Main Interface
![Link Calculator Main Interface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/link-assistant/calculator/issue-1-177867357bb4/docs/screenshots/calculator-main.png)

## Features

### Expression Parser
- Arithmetic operations: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` with proper precedence
- Parentheses for grouping: `(2 + 3) * 4`
- Negative numbers: `-5 + 3`
- Decimal precision using `rust_decimal`

### DateTime Support
- Multiple date formats: ISO (`2026-01-22`), US (`01/22/2026`), European (`22/01/2026`)
- Month names: `Jan 22, 2026`, `22 Jan 2026`
- Time formats: `8:59am`, `14:30`, with timezone support (`8:59am UTC`)
- DateTime arithmetic: `(Jan 27, 8:59am UTC) - (Jan 25, 12:51pm UTC)`

### Currency Support
- Currency amounts: `84 USD`, `34 EUR`
- Currency arithmetic with conversion: `100 USD + 50 EUR`
- Temporal awareness: `84 USD - 34 EUR at 22 Jan 2026`
- Support for 50+ currencies including major world currencies, precious metals, and cryptocurrencies

### Links Notation
- All expressions represented in links-notation format
- Step-by-step calculation explanations
- Issue prefill links for unrecognized input

## Technical Implementation

### Rust WASM Core (`src/`)
- `grammar/` - Lexer and recursive descent parser
- `types/` - Value, Decimal, DateTime, Currency, Unit types
- `lino/` - Links notation representation
- `error/` - Error types with thiserror
- `wasm.rs` - WebAssembly bindings

### React Frontend (`web/`)
- Vite + TypeScript + React 18
- Web Worker for non-blocking WASM calculations
- Responsive design with real-time results
- Example expressions for quick testing

### CI/CD (`.github/workflows/`)
- `ci.yml` - Tests, linting, formatting, WASM build
- `deploy.yml` - GitHub Pages deployment
